name: Ilomba
body:
ILOMBA
CR 2

With bone-white fangs, smooth shadowy scales, and iridescent eyes, this large sleek snake slithers with flowing grace.

XP 600
NE Medium outsider (evil, native)
Init +3; Senses blindsight 10 ft., darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +12

DEFENSE

AC 14, touch 13, flat-footed 11 (+3 Dex, +1 natural)
hp 19 (3d10+3)
Fort +2, Ref +6, Will +2
Immune disease, poison

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., swim 30 ft.
Melee bite +4 (1d6+1 plus consume shadow and drain life)
Special Attacks consume shadow, drain life
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 3rd; concentration +5)

At will—alter self (form of master only)

STATISTICS

Str 13, Dex 16, Con 13, Int 12, Wis 8, Cha 15
Base Atk +3; CMB +4; CMD 17 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Deceitful, Skill Focus (Perception)
Skills Acrobatics +9, Bluff +10, Disguise +10, Perception +12, Sense Motive +5, Stealth +13, Swim +15; Racial Modifiers +4 Perception, +4 Stealth
Languages Common, one language known by master; telepathy 100 ft. (master only)
SQ hunger, soul bond

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Consume Shadow (Su)

As a standard action or when it hits with a bite attack, an ilomba can target a living sentient creature (one with Intelligence 3 or more) within its reach that isn’t an ooze or plant. The creature must succeed at a DC 13 Will save or lose its shadow and become frightened for 1 minute. Each round at the end of its turn, the creature may attempt a new saving throw to end this effect. A creature that is immune to fear can still lose its shadow. The frightened aspect is a mind-affecting fear effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Drain Life (Su)

As a standard action, the ilomba targets a creature within 30 feet that is currently affected by its consume shadow ability. The target takes 1d8+3 negative energy damage and gains 1 temporary negative level. A successful DC 13 Fortitude save halves the damage and negates the negative level. This negative level never becomes permanent, and in addition to other methods, it can be removed with remove curse.

The ilomba can also activate this ability as an immediate action after hitting a creature affected by its consume shadow ability with a bite attack—including cases where the target fails its saving throw against consume shadow from the same bite attack. This is a curse effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Hunger (Su)

The ilomba hungers for flesh, souls, and lives. If an ilomba doesn’t deal a negative level or kill a creature with its drain life ability during a week, its master gains 1 temporary negative level which cannot be removed until the ilomba feeds.

Soul Bond (Su)

The ilomba and its master share their life essence. If the ilomba or its master dies, the other must succeed at a DC 13 Fort save or be reduced to 0 hit points, or take 2d8+3 damage if the save succeeds. The save DC is Charisma-based.

After killing a creature with its drain life ability, the ilomba may slither over its master’s body for 1 minute granting immunity to disease and +2 profane bonus to Constitution. These benefits last for 1 week. A master who continually receives these benefits for several years lives a long life, their maximum age increases to the highest number of years possible for their race, as long as they feed the ilomba’s hunger.

ECOLOGY

The ilomba (also malomba) is a sorcerous serpent created by a witch doctor using a mixture of magical herbs, fingernails, and blood, often to serve as a familiar spirit for powerful sorcerers. Ilombas prefer to make nests in banks of reeds alongside slow-moving rivers, but they will live wherever their masters command.

The ilomba is known for its destructive powers and its ability to resemble its owner, sharing their features and emotions. It is used to kill enemies or steal resources, but its power comes at a steep price: a symbiotic bond of power and pain with its owner. These darker aspects of witchcraft and sorcery highlight the dangers of seeking power through magic. Its symbiotic bond with its owner serves as a cautionary tale about the consequences of wielding such power. The ilomba can be a formidable foe or a powerful ally, depending on how its master chooses to utilize it, though their bond requires a ritual of reverence between the ilomba and its master.

Ilombas seek to consume the lives and souls of intelligent creatures, snaring their shadows and draining their life away.

It may demand its master provide such sustenance, or it can serve as an assassin at their master’s behest, feasting on flesh and even swallowing prey whole. Ilombas often crawl back to their masters after a killing, creeping over their master’s body and licking them to share the essence of the kill.
